use: Texted or said when you're close; often with yo, or kara to mean so hang on.

example.romaji: mou sugu tsuku yo. ato gofun.
example.ja: もうすぐ着くよ。あと5分。
example.english: I'm almost there. Five more minutes.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、もうすぐ着きます。

notes: Mou sugu means very soon and works with other verbs: mou sugu owaru (almost done).

politeJa: どこで会いましょうか
use: Asked when making plans; answer with a place, or suggest one: eki de ii?

example.romaji: doyoubi, doko de au? shibuya de ii?
example.ja: 土曜日、どこで会う？渋谷でいい？
example.english: Where shall we meet on Saturday? Is Shibuya okay?

examplePolite.romaji: ashita wa doko de aimashou ka?
examplePolite.ja: 明日はどこで会いましょうか？

notes: Machiawase is the arrangement to meet; machiawase basho is the meeting spot.

politeJa: 先に行っていてください
english: go on ahead; go without me
use: Said when you'll catch up later; the other person may answer jaa, matteru ne.

example.ja: 忘れ物した。先に行ってて！
example.english: I forgot something. Go on ahead!

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, saki ni itte ite kudasai. sugu oikakemasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、先に行っていてください。すぐ追いかけます。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, please go on ahead. I'll catch up soon.

notes: Don't mix it up with osaki ni, which you say when you leave before others.

src: 電話出られなくてごめん
ja: 電話出られなくてごめん
kana: でんわでられなくてごめん
politeJa: お電話に出られずすみませんでした
use: Said or texted when you call back after missing someone's call.

example.romaji: denwa derarenakute gomen. dou shita no?
example.ja: 電話出られなくてごめん。どうしたの？
example.english: Sorry I missed your call. What's up?

examplePolite.romaji: sakki wa odenwa ni derarezu sumimasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: さっきはお電話に出られずすみませんでした。
examplePolite.english: Sorry I couldn't take your call earlier.

notes: Denwa ni deru means answer the phone; casual speech drops the ni.

english: what are you up to?; what are you doing now?
use: An opening text or call to a friend or partner, often before inviting them out.

example.romaji: ima nani shiteru? hima nara gohan ikanai?
example.ja: 今何してる？暇ならご飯行かない？
example.english: What are you up to? If you're free, want to grab food?

notes: A common answer is betsu ni or nanimo shitenai (nothing much).

english: did you wait long?; have you been waiting?
use: Asked when you meet someone who got there first; the classic answer is uun, ima kita tokoro (no, I just got here).

example.romaji: gomen, matta? uun, ima kita tokoro.
example.ja: ごめん、待った？ううん、今来たところ。
example.english: Sorry, did you wait long? No, I just got here.

notes: Shouted, matta! means hold on! or wait!

english: I can't make it after all
use: Said to cancel a plan you agreed to, usually with gomen and a short reason.

example.romaji: gomen, kyuu ni shigoto ga haitte ikenaku natta.
example.ja: ごめん、急に仕事が入って行けなくなった。
example.english: Sorry, something came up at work and I can't make it.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、明日行けなくなりました。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I can't make it tomorrow after all.

notes: The -naku natta ending says things changed, which sounds softer than a flat ikenai.

english: when works for you?; when's good?
use: Asked when setting a date; answer with a day + ga ii, or X wa dou?

example.romaji: kondo nomi ni ikou yo. itsu ga ii?
example.ja: 今度飲みに行こうよ。いつがいい？
example.english: Let's go for a drink sometime. When works for you?

examplePolite.romaji: uchiawase wa itsu ga ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 打ち合わせはいつがいいですか？
examplePolite.english: When is good for the meeting?

notes: At work, itsu ga yoroshii desu ka is more polite.

english: is now a good time?; got a minute?
use: Asked at the start of a call or before interrupting someone; answer un, daijoubu or gomen, ato de.

example.romaji: moshimoshi, ima daijoubu? chotto kikitai koto ga atte.
example.ja: もしもし、今大丈夫？ちょっと聞きたいことがあって。
example.english: Hi, is now a good time? There's something I want to ask.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, ima daijoubu desu ka? sugu sumimasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、今大丈夫ですか？すぐ済みます。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, do you have a moment? It won't take long.

notes: To a boss or client, ima ojikan yoroshii desu ka is safer.

use: LINE is Japan's main messaging app; said at a goodbye or when you want an update.

example.english: Message me when you get there.

examplePolite.ja: 何かあったらLINEください。
examplePolite.english: Message me if anything comes up.

notes: LINE works as a suru verb: rain suru, rain shita. Meeru shite is the older email version.

use: Asked once you've picked a day; answer with a time, or suggest one: rokuji wa dou?

example.romaji: doyoubi ne. jaa, nanji ga ii?
example.ja: 土曜日ね。じゃあ、何時がいい？
example.english: Saturday, then. So what time works for you?

examplePolite.romaji: ashita wa nanji ga ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 明日は何時がいいですか？
examplePolite.english: What time is good for you tomorrow?

notes: Nanji is what time; don't confuse it with nanjikan (how many hours).

kana: ラインこうかんしよう
use: Said to someone new you want to keep in touch with; you then scan each other's QR code.

example.romaji: kyou tanoshikatta! rain koukan shiyou yo.
example.ja: 今日楽しかった！LINE交換しようよ。
example.english: Today was fun! Let's swap LINE.

examplePolite.ja: よかったら、LINE交換しませんか？
examplePolite.english: If you like, shall we exchange LINE contacts?

notes: Renrakusaki koukan is the general version: swapping contact details.

use: Said to warn that a call or chat may cut off soon.

example.romaji: yabai, juuden kiresou. ato de kakenaosu ne.
example.ja: やばい、充電切れそう。後でかけ直すね。
example.english: Ugh, my battery's about to die. I'll call you back.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, juuden ga kiresou desu. ato de renraku shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、充電が切れそうです。後で連絡します。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, my battery's almost dead. I'll get in touch later.

notes: Juuden kireta means it died; a charger is juudenki.
